title: HIV, AIDS and population

blocks.heading: HIV, AIDS and population
blocks.text: HIV is a virus affecting the immune system; AIDS is an advanced stage of untreated HIV infection. Effective treatment and accessible support change health outcomes. Illness and premature deaths can affect household care, age patterns and livelihoods, but do not assume HIV means immediate death or inability to work. Health and population judgements need evidence and non-stigmatising language.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the measure
blocks.text: Describe this fictional service series: access to ongoing HIV care rises from 50% to 80% of an eligible group while recorded missed-work days fall from 200 to 120 under the stated definitions. Wider care access accompanies 80 fewer missed days and a 30-percentage-point coverage gain. The association supports investigating access and participation, but does not establish treatment caused the whole work change.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Health evidence
blocks.text: [WHO’s HIV fact sheet](https://www.who.int/en/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/hiv-aids), checked 20 October 2026, distinguishes HIV from AIDS and explains the role of effective treatment. Ordinary social contact does not transmit HIV. This is conceptual health education, not an individual diagnosis or treatment instruction.

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
